get_continent_totals.description: Read the final COVID-19 totals for each of the six continents Worldometers groups countries into, or for one of them: cases, deaths, recoveries, tests and population, the per-million figures, and the countries each one covers. Largest first, by cases. Figures are as they stood on 13 April 2024, when Worldometers stopped updating.
get_continent_totals.display_str_template: Get COVID-19 totals by continent from disease.sh.

mock_response.note: Worldometers stopped updating its COVID-19 figures on 13 April 2024 because most countries had stopped reporting, so these are its final published totals. Active and critical cases are as they stood then.
mock_response.summary: Europe recorded the most COVID-19 cases, 253,406,198, before Worldometers stopped updating on 13 April 2024.

get_country_history.description: Read how COVID-19 cases and deaths rose in a country, one of its provinces, or the whole world - day by day, week by week or month by month - from Johns Hopkins University's series, which runs from 22 January 2020 to 9 March 2023. Each period carries its new cases and deaths as well as the running totals, and the answer names the worst one. Recoveries are included until Johns Hopkins stopped counting them in August 2021.
get_country_history.display_str_template: Get a COVID-19 history from disease.sh.

mock_response.note: Johns Hopkins University stopped updating its COVID-19 data on 10 March 2023, and stopped counting recoveries on 5 August 2021.
mock_response.summary: Italy recorded 8,516,671 new COVID-19 cases and 21,981 deaths between 1 January 2022 and 31 March 2022, for running totals of 14,642,354 cases and 159,383 deaths. The most new cases came in January 2022: 4,857,433.

get_country_history.name: get_country_history

parameters.description: The country to read, by name ('Italy'), two-letter code ('IT') or three-letter code ('ITA'). Leave empty for the whole world.
parameters.name: country

parameters.description: Narrow to one province or state of the country, as Johns Hopkins split it: Canada's provinces, Australia's states, China's provinces, and the overseas territories of France, the Netherlands, Denmark and the UK. Leave empty for the whole country. For US states use 'Get US history' instead.
parameters.name: province

parameters.description: The first day to include. Leave empty to start where the data starts.
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: The last day to include. Leave empty to run to the end of the data; every series here has stopped, so there is nothing more recent.
parameters.name: end

parameters.description: How to group the days. A week or month carries its new cases and deaths added up, and the running totals as of its last day. Weeks run Monday to Sunday. Defaults to weekly.
parameters.name: interval

get_mobility_trends.description: Read how much people drove, walked and took public transit through the pandemic, from Apple Maps route requests, as the percentage change against 13 January 2020 - for a country, or one of its regions or cities. Averaged by day, week or month, with the lowest point named. Apple published these from January 2020 to 12 April 2022.

mock_response.note: Apple stopped publishing its Mobility Trends Reports in April 2022; the last day is 12 April 2022. Each figure is the percentage change in route requests from Apple Maps against 13 January 2020.
mock_response.summary: Between 1 March 2020 and 31 May 2020, Apple Maps requests in USA averaged driving -18.9%, walking -30%, transit -61.2% against January 2020. The lowest point was transit on 12 April 2020, at -80.9%.

get_vaccinations.description: Read how many COVID-19 vaccine doses had been given, and how fast, in a country, a US state or the whole world, from Our World in Data: the running total, doses per 100 people, and the doses given in each day, week or month. The figures run from December 2020 to August 2024 (May 2023 for US states), and each place stops on the day it last reported, returned as 'lastReported'; disease.sh's own copy repeats the last figure every day since, and that padding is cut off.

mock_response.note: Our World in Data has stopped collecting vaccination figures. Each place stops on the day it last reported, which is given as 'lastReported'. Doses per hundred people is a whole number, rounded down, and 'dailyAverage' is Our World in Data's seven-day average of doses a day.
mock_response.summary: Italy had given 52,191,122 COVID-19 vaccine doses by 30 June 2021, 88 for every 100 people, 52,150,455 of them from 1 January 2021.

Follow one variant to see it rise and fall. Covers the 30 EU and EEA countries until week 47 of 2023.

Narrow it to one continent, or leave out small countries so a few micro-states do not lead every per-person ranking. A country that never reported the chosen figure is counted and left out, not ranked as zero. Figures are as they stood on 13 April 2024, when Worldometers stopped updating.

description: Read COVID-19 statistics from disease.sh, the open-source API that gathers them from Worldometers, Johns Hopkins University, The New York Times, Our World in Data, the ECDC and Apple: the final totals for the world, every country, continent and US state; how cases and deaths rose day by day in a country, province, state or county; vaccine doses given; which variants were circulating in Europe; and how much people moved about. Every source has now stopped publishing, so each answer names its source and its last day. No account or API key required.
